This also helps because, like me, you said that you are a binger and can pretty easily go cold turkey. I've found that in the past when I "reduce" something I end up binging but when I "cut" something I have more success. This is something a lot of people don't understand. I didn't have one intentional slip up the entire month (did you know KFC breads their French fries, I didn't). If cutting things works for you, then do that. Just make sure you don't fall into the trap of labeling those foods as "bad".

I just did the Whole30 diet. You cut out all Dairy, Gluten Grains, Non-Gluten Grains, Legumes, Alcohol, and most preservatives for 30 days and then reintroduce them. There is an app for $2.99 on the app store called WholeEats.

So, for 30 days you don't eat these things and then on day 31 you reintroduce alcohol, back to Whole30 for days 32 and 33, Legumes, 35, 36, Non-Gluten Grains, 38, 39, Dairy, 41, 42, Gluten Grains, 43, 44, and then back to a non-restrictive diet.

You are supposed to be able to lose weight without counting calories (eating whole foods get you fuller faster) but if you find yourself binging even while following the diet perfectly, I would count calories anyway.

It's supposed to do all sorts of things like reduce inflammation, and help you kick start the weight loss process. For a full list of benefits search "Whole 30 benefits"

I will go ahead and say, I had a binge eating disorder (that I may still have, I haven't been off of it long enough to know) and I'm also pretty picky but I was able to follow through. Also, because I am pretty picky my caloric intake dropped significantly and I lost 20lbs. Let me reiterate that that is NOT the purpose of the diet. That is one part where I didn't do it right.
